q: Some objects such as the sun, the stars, fluorescent lamps and candles make their own light. These sources are called ____.
e: Some objects such as the sun, the stars, fluorescent lamps and candles make their own light. These sources are called luminous sources. Luminous sources names some objects such as the sun, the stars, fluorescent lamps and candles make their own light. These sources.

q: Most objects do not emit their own light but reflect light from luminous sources. They are ____.
e: Most objects do not emit their own light but reflect light from luminous sources. They are non-luminous objects. The physics in this sentence is built around non-luminous objects.

q: The sun is the chief source of ____.
e: The sun is the chief source of light. The physics in this sentence is built around light.

q: The fact that light coming from the sun passes through the empty space on its way to the earth shows that light can travel through ____.
e: The fact that light coming from the sun passes through the empty space on its way to the earth shows that light can travel through vacuum. Vacuum here means a space emptied of air so electrons can travel freely in a tube.

q: All the forms of electromagnetic radiation, including light, travel at a speed of $3 \times 10^8$ m/s in a ____.
e: All the forms of electromagnetic radiation, including light, travel at a speed of $3 \times 10^8$ m/s in a vacuum. Vacuum here means a space emptied of air so electrons can travel freely in a tube.

q: When light is incident on the surface of an object some of the light is sent back and this phenomenon is called ____.
e: When light is incident on the surface of an object some of the light is sent back and this phenomenon is called reflection of light. Reflection of light here means light bouncing back from a surface. On reflection, the angle of incidence equals the angle of reflection.

q: A ray of light is a path along which the light ____.
e: A ray of light is a path along which the light travels. Distance grows with the path, even if you return to the start.

q: A beam of light is a collection of ____.
e: A beam of light is a collection of rays of light. The physics in this sentence is built around rays of light.

q: Searchlights used in trains and lighthouses emit ____.
e: Searchlights used in trains and lighthouses emit parallel beam of light. The physics in this sentence is built around parallel beam of light.

q: A beam emitted by a light bulb is a ____.
e: A beam emitted by a light bulb is a divergent beam. The physics in this sentence is built around divergent beam.

q: In Figure 8.4, a ray which represents the incident light is an ____.
e: In Figure 8.4, a ray which represents the incident light is an incident ray (AO). The physics in this sentence is built around incident ray (AO).

q: A line perpendicular to the surface at the point of incidence is called ____.
e: A line perpendicular to the surface at the point of incidence is called normal (NO). Normal (NO) names a line perpendicular to the surface at the point of incidence.

q: A ray which represents the reflected light is a ____.
e: A ray which represents the reflected light is a reflected ray (OB). The physics in this sentence is built around reflected ray (OB).

q: An angle between the incident ray and the normal is an ____.
e: An angle between the incident ray and the normal is an angle of incidence (i). The physics in this sentence is built around angle of incidence (i).

q: An angle between the reflected ray and the normal is an ____.
e: An angle between the reflected ray and the normal is an angle of reflection (r). Angle of reflection (r) here means light bouncing back from a surface.

q: The incident ray, the reflected ray and the normal all lie in the same ____.
e: The incident ray, the reflected ray and the normal all lie in the same plane. The physics in this sentence is built around plane.

q: The angle of incidence is equal to the ____.
e: The angle of incidence is equal to the angle of reflection. Angle of reflection here means light bouncing back from a surface.

q: Laws of reflection are true for all reflecting surfaces for plane mirrors as well as ____.
e: Laws of reflection are true for all reflecting surfaces for plane mirrors as well as curved mirrors. Curved mirrors here means a bent path, which light does not take in a uniform medium. On reflection, the angle of incidence equals the angle of reflection.
